newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison Petroleums posts record results.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Petroleums posts record results.

text.p: Morrison Petroleums Ltd, target of a C$652 million hostile takeover bid from Canadian 88 Energy Corp, on Wednesday made good on a promise to shareholders by reporting record 1996 financial results.

For the full year, Morrison earned C$36.2 million or C$0.54 per share, up from 17.2 million or C$0.26 per share in 1995. Cash flow climbed to C$100.2 million or C$1.47 per share in 1996 from C$82.8 million or C$1.25 per share a year earlier.
The company said natural gas production rose 35 percent in 1996 to an average 87.9 million cubic feet per day.
Oil and natural gas liquids production, however, fell 16 percent to 11,908 barrels per day.
Morrison said proven plus propable reserves at December 31 rose 39 percent to 88.5 million barrels of oil equivalent from the year-earlier total of 63.7 million BOE.
The reserves total included a 16 percent rise in oil and natural gas liquids to 22.6 million barrels and a 23 percent jump in gas to 413.4 billion cubic feet, Morrison said.

The company said it made asset dispositions in the fourth quarter garnering proceeds of C$77 million. Also, the expected close of its royalty trust formation based on cash flow from an Alberta gas plant and British Columbia oil pipeline was expected to bring in another C$180 million.

Morrison said its year-end working capital totalled C$49 million and net debt was valued at C$53 million. By the end of January, when all transactions are slated to close, the company's debt would be about C$10 million, Morrison said.
